system:
You are the Met office reviewer, standing in for the national meteorological centre (hazard facts). You check that the alert says what the hazard bulletin says: the same hazard, the same times, the same places, severity and certainty no higher or lower than the bulletin supports, and no unverified report in the alert.
You see only the event inputs (marked verified or unverified) and the English alert fields. You cannot approve or send the alert; people decide.

Review the alert within your mandate only. Decide:
- "agree": nothing within your mandate is wrong;
- "object": something is wrong and the drafter can fix it (say how in `fix`);
- "escalate": something is wrong that needs a decision by a person or a higher authority.

Every objection needs evidence. Each evidence item is a word-for-word quote (at least 5 words for a
clause, at least 3 for the alert or inputs) from either a knowledge base clause shown to you (kind
"clause", ref = its id) or the material you were shown (kind "view", ref = the field name). Quotes are
checked by code; an objection with no quote that matches is thrown away. Do not object to things
outside your mandate. Do not repeat the same issue twice. Issues listed under `recorded_gaps` are already
reported to the approvers on every alert; do not object to them again.
If you have a concern but none of the clauses shown supports it, put it in `no_basis` instead.

data.summary: The verified NCM bulletin reports an active dust hazard from 14:55 to 19:00 on 4 March 2026. In that bulletin, NCM urges caution while driving. The alert instead tells the public to disregard an earlier alert and says no action is needed. This contradicts the verified hazard. The structured fields (Observed/Immediate/Moderate) also conflict with the retraction text. A person must decide whether an earlier message really was sent in error and should be cancelled. Either way, the alert must not tell the public that no action is needed while the NCM warning is in force. The unverified dam rumour is correctly left out.

objections.issue: The alert tells the public to disregard the weather alert and that no action is needed. The verified NCM bulletin says blowing dust and reduced visibility are ongoing until 19:00 and urges caution. The alert therefore contradicts the verified hazard and could lead people to drop precautions during an active warning. Whether an earlier alert was actually erroneous cannot be confirmed from the inputs, so a person must decide.
objections.fix: A person should confirm whether an earlier message was sent in error. If it was, issue a cancel (msgType Cancel referencing that message). The cancel should still state that the NCM dust warning remains active until 19:00. If no earlier alert was erroneous, replace the text with the bulletin content: fresh to strong northwesterly winds causing blowing dust and sand; visibility below 2,000 metres in some coastal and inland areas; from 14:55 until 19:00 today; take caution when driving on open roads.

objections.issue: The certainty, urgency and severity fields describe an observed, immediate hazard. The headline and description say the alert was sent in error. The alert therefore gives contradictory signals about whether the hazard exists.
objections.fix: Make the fields and the text consistent. If this is a hazard alert, keep Observed/Immediate/Moderate and use bulletin-based text. If it is a cancellation, structure it as a Cancel and do not present it as an observed hazard alert.
